title: Review: the cost of the cog shell gate from noise replicates on fresh seeds 6 and 7 (3 and 0 cogs at t=500, against 12 and 18 ungated). A uniformly slow medium from t=0 costs the same (3 and 1).
summary: Ran c18's lcn-cog world.py from full-domain noise to t=500 (labkit, 192^2, 100 frames x 50 steps) on seeds 6 and 7. With beta=betaW=8 (gated/), cogs nucleate in the transient (max 23 and 28 components) but most fade by t~110-215: final 3 and 0, persistent 3 and 0 (gated/seed6/sheet.png). Without the gate (ungated/): final 12 and 18, persistent 12 and 18. The finding's limit asks whether uniformly low D from t=0 has the same cost. With D=DW=0.0007 everywhere (slowD/, the in-shell value c18 matched): final 3 and 1, persistent 4 and 1. So the gate's cost at birth is the cost of slow transport, consistent with c18's finding that the gate is a slow medium.

observations.F: gated/seed6/FACTS.md final 3 (persistent 3), gated/seed7/FACTS.md final 0; ungated/seed6 final 12, ungated/seed7 final 18; slowD/seed6 final 3, slowD/seed7 final 1; gated/seed6/sheet.png t=45-215: young cogs fade, 3 remain

controls_run.F: ungated/seed6, ungated/seed7 (beta=betaW=0); extra arm slowD/seed6, slowD/seed7 (D=DW=0.0007 uniform)

verdicts.limitation: t=500 and one gate strength, as in the finding. The slow-D arm shows the cost is not specific to the gate.
